assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based drugs is a rare complete arc from basic peptide biology to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with very large and still growing clinical and societal impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology, active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and intestinotrophic GLP-2, translational advocacy) and Knudsen (long-acting analogues, liraglutide/semaglutide) form a coherent three-person configuration. Svetlana Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide and its credit is contested, and I leave her out only because of the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy confirmed in large independent outcome trials across several drug classes; timing is highly appropriate and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: How to weigh the disputed early peptide-identification credit (Mojsov, Habener group) against physiology and drug development.
Industry versus academic credit inside a single prize.
Long-term safety questions are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells that durably eradicate refractory B-cell malignancies established a new therapeutic modality, with strong originality and clear clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CD28-costimulated CAR design), June (4-1BB CAR and the first durable clinical responses) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, early clinical CAR and TIL work) are the natural trio. Eshhar and others are not on the supplied list, so the credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation; the field is mature for hematologic cancers, less so for solid tumors.
uncertainties: Missing foundational contributors in the supplied credit.
Limited benefit in solid tumors; toxicity and manufacturing burden.
Whether Rosenberg's role is better framed as adoptive therapy generally.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has reshaped experimental brain research, with deep originality and wide adoption.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Deisseroth, Boyden; Miesenböck earlier) leave a hard six-way allocation. I propose a discovery-plus-implementation configuration, which inevitably excludes deserving people.
assessment.maturity: Technique is thoroughly validated and ubiquitous; clinical translation (retinal optogenetic vision restoration) is early, but the tool value is mature.
uncertainties: Severe attribution crowding and priority disputes.
Method/tool rather than disease-mechanism discovery, which may weigh differently for a Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signaling logic that links ER stress to cell fate and disease, with fundamental originality.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the Ire1/Hac1 (XBP1) signaling pathway in yeast, a clean two-person credit; other contributors (Ron, Kaufman, Schekman and Sambrook lineage) are not supplied.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly in yeast and mammals; disease relevance (cancer, neurodegeneration, diabetes) is increasingly supported and therapeutic translation is emerging.
uncertainties: Whether other pathway contributors (PERK, ATF6 arms) deserve recognition.
Clinical translation is not yet decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense therapy for SMA is a clear mechanistic and clinical triumph, converting a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one, and validates antisense RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 exon 7 splicing mechanism and the antisense strategy with Bennett's Ionis platform and medicinal chemistry leading to nusinersen; two-person credit is sensible, though others (Hua, Singh) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up and independent confirmation; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Contributions of Ionis and academic co-workers are not fully reflected.
Overlap with other SMA therapies such as gene therapy and risdiplam.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified the cytosolic DNA sensing mechanism in innate immunity, linking infection, autoimmunity and cancer immunity with strong conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are also credited, but I regard Chen and Barber as decisive. Other independent work (Vance, Patel, Hornung) is not on the supplied list, which leaves credit uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Robustly confirmed and extended in many labs; therapeutic agonists and antagonists remain in clinical development.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet established.
Allocation of credit among STING discoverers and other cyclic dinucleotide researchers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identification as the central nutrient and growth regulator is a foundational finding with broad relevance to cancer, metabolism, aging and transplantation.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and its role in growth control; Schreiber and Sabatini contributed to rapamycin target and mTORC1 nutrient sensing, but I consider Hall the decisive discoverer. Credit for mTOR in mammals is shared and potentially contentious.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mature; rapalog clinical use exists, with ongoing translational expansion.
uncertainties: Attribution complexity regarding mammalian mTOR identification.
Whether a single-person prize is appropriate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib for BCR-ABL-driven CML showed that targeted kinase inhibition can transform an incurable cancer, a paradigm for precision oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery and project), Druker (clinical development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a defensible trio; Nowell, Rowley, Witte and Ben-Neriah on the underlying biology are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of survival data; recognition is not premature but the field has already received substantial prizes.
uncertainties: Upstream contributors to BCR-ABL biology are missing from the supplied credit.
Risk of recognizing translation while underlying biology goes unrewarded.
